title: The tropical Pacific closes the 1982-2022 SST radiation-pattern gap to 31 CMIP6 models under mean-preserving linear replacement
abstract: We tested which SST regions supply the remaining radiation-pattern gap between observations and 112 members of 31 CMIP6 models. We used published 5-degree trend maps, eight distinct raw or corrected SST patterns, and five atmosphere-model response maps. Each regional replacement keeps full-mask mean warming fixed. For 1982-2022, replacing the tropical Pacific pattern at 30S-30N removes 107-139% of the gap in the mean response. The outside-Pacific part offsets some of the gap and lies within the simulated member range for every tested pattern and primary response map. The equatorial strip at 10S-10N removes only 44-63%. Matching only two broad west/east Pacific means removes 61-79%. The strict coastal mask and 1982-2014 period retain Pacific dominance. Without uniform mean compensation, its share is 78-102% in the mean response. Thus the precise share depends on the replacement rule. This adds a regional budget of the artifact-tested gap, not a new observation or coupled-model experiment. It does not identify the cause of the Pacific pattern, rule out remote ocean effects, or estimate Earth feedback. Static linear responses, a fixed 60S-60N ice-free mask, model surface temperature and common data errors limit the result. Code, exact retrieval hashes, scalar evidence and numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Tropical Pacific replacement removes the mean radiation-pattern gap. Values use five response maps and keep full-mask mean warming fixed. Eight distinct SST patterns are shown. The right panel compares outside-Pacific values with the member distribution. Shading marks central 95% member percentiles, not a confidence interval.
Signed regional budget and fixed broad-mean replacements. Ranges show product spread, not confidence intervals. The broad-region tests are exploratory.
